analyst_view.overall: Early view: Benfica travel to Madeira on Saturday 5 December, five days after hosting Famalicão and five before a Europa League game at OFI Crete. Nacional, 13th, have changed coach again (João Henriques, their third this season) and have won their last two home league games 1-0, against Braga and Académico Viseu. Madeira weather has already caused postponements this month, which is worth watching.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: Nacional's recent home wins came by 1-0 with a deep, physical defence, and Académico's coach said they looked like a team that had 'shut the door on its goal'. Benfica should win, but their rotation and a crowded week point to a narrower score.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, 6.5 for Benfica. Nacional defend deep and Benfica's habit is to win lots of corners against low blocks; they had ten at Estrela. I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. I lean a little higher: Nacional's recent wins were built on a physical approach, and Marco Silva was booked for protests at Estrela. A home side defending for 90 minutes against Benfica tends to collect bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, which looks high. Benfica managed 15 shots at Estrela with 62% possession, and Nacional's deep block limits clear attempts. Their own counter-attacks will be few.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Benfica had only 5 on target at Estrela, and Nacional crowd the box. I lean lower.
